title: the P08 documents: the payments runbook with 'When the Moyasar keys arrive', operations, the privacy data map and local development
readFirst: PLANS/P08-CONTRACT.md in full (it is the fact the documents describe, with the 'As built' notes), and every round file in artifacts/acceptance/P08/rounds/ for what was built and the orchestrator's rulings (the residuals and ceilings each one records)
artifacts/acceptance/P08/moyasar-docs-2026-10-02.md and artifacts/acceptance/P08/moyasar-sandbox-2026-10-02.md (what the documentation says and what the sandbox answered)
docs/payments-runbook.md, docs/operations.md, docs/privacy-data-map.md, docs/development.md as they are: extend them in their own voice and structure; keep every existing section that is still true

the code the documents describe, to check every name and number against it: supabase/migrations/2026100*.sql (every P08 function, job and its schedule in `cron.schedule`), supabase/functions/_shared/payments.ts, payments/moyasar.ts, checkout.ts, orders.ts, download.ts, notify.ts, refunds.ts, disputes.ts, paid-files.ts, jobs.ts, outbox.ts, admin.ts, tests/support/moyasar-emulator.ts, scripts/local-env.mjs, scripts/backup.mjs, scripts/restore-check.mjs, .env.example, src/components/admin/* (the screens the owner uses)
PLANS/DECISIONS.md (D34, D38, D42, D45) and PLANS/ISSUES.md (I32, I40, I48) for the names to cite
brief:
Write the P08 documents. They are read by Anas (the owner's routine), by the next developer (runbook, development) and at a privacy request. Plain, exact, in English like the existing docs, with the Arabic of a button or a sentence quoted as the screen shows it. Every function, job, schedule, limit, code and column you name must exist in the code as you name it: check each against the source, and never describe something that is not built. No invented price, policy, payment, approval or gate closure; E02 and E03 stay open and the documents say so.

1. `docs/payments-runbook.md`: keep the source tables and the emulator section; add:
- 'How a payment settles': the invoice step, the webhook (`secret_token` in the body, stored before the reply), the callback, the return page's verify, the reconciliation job and its leases and back-off, the late payment, review payments, mode checks; in prose and one short table of who may move what.
- 'Refunds': the order of operations (fetch the provider's total first, reserve, one in flight, `refund_result`, `refund_settle`'s branches, the 15-minute rule, external refunds and voids recorded from the dashboard).
- 'Disputes and payouts': recorded by hand from Moyasar's emails and settlement files, append-only, never a refund.
- 'Switching from the emulator to the real sandbox, then to live': exactly the environment variables of contract section 1 (names only), the dashboard webhook, the sandbox fence and `PAYMENTS_TEST_ACCESS_CODE`, and that it is configuration only.
- 'When the Moyasar keys arrive': the exact things Anas must bring (the secret key per mode, the webhook secret he sets in the dashboard, the account's activation for live, the publishable key only if a later page needs it: say whether anything uses it today), then the short list of sandbox runs that close E02, each with what to record: a book purchase, a non-book purchase, a failed payment, 3-D Secure, a cancelled checkout, a refund, Apple Pay on a supported device, plus every still-open item of contract section 2's list (items 3, 6 to 11, 13, and the rest of 4, 5 and 14), each named with the question it answers. Say that nothing here closes E02 or E03 until those runs are recorded.
2. `docs/operations.md`: add P08 sections in the existing voice: the owner's daily routine for orders (the home alerts, `/admin/orders` and its filters, shipping with the signed checklist, returns and the restock rule: goods come back on sale only through a received return, a refund never restocks), refunds and the step-up, the reconciliation screen (each section and what to do), review payments, disputes, the paid-file upload and what happens to waiting orders, availability sign-ups and notices, preorders (off at opening on Anas's word, how to turn one on, the capacity, netting confirmed preorders out of real stock), the checkout switch, the mail budget's three tiers and caps (contract section 8), every new pg_cron job with its schedule added to 'Every pg_cron job (the restore checklist)', the residuals recorded in the contract and the round files (the per-email hold removed and its residual, section 13.1; the asset left under `assets/` with no row and the query that lists it; the checkout page's 1.1 KiB of budget headroom), and the hosted checks still owed (I32: CORS of `orders` and `download`, Range and `nosniff` on the file reply, the `_headers` rules of `/orders`, `/checkout/return` and `/notify/*`).
3. `docs/privacy-data-map.md`: the buyer rows P08 adds to the data map (payment attempts with only the fields kept, review payments, webhook events with no body, entitlements, download tokens (hashes), fulfilments with carrier and tracking, return requests with the reason, refunds, disputes, notifications with their consent revision, the variant availability rows, the outbox payloads with ids only, the throttle hashes P08 adds), each with why, who can read it and how long it stays (the purges and their clocks, as built); the buyer's browser storage P08 adds (the order access pair in sessionStorage, the sandbox access code, the notification token kept in memory only); the providers (Moyasar: what it receives, which is the amount, the order number and the attempt id, and never the buyer's name, email, phone or address). Then replace the 'A buyer' paragraph with the request runbook: see or export with `privacy_buyer_export`, erase with `privacy_buyer_erase` (run as the migration role, the reasons an order is kept: `ACCOUNTING_RETENTION`, `OPEN_HOLD`, `PAYMENT_RECORDS`), the deletion ledger line, and what stays (paid orders under the accounting retention E08 sets).
4. `docs/development.md`: a 'Payments locally (P08)' section: `pnpm db:env` and the local payment values (names, and that they are refused in a built export), `pnpm emulator` and its control routes in one paragraph pointing at the runbook, the local stack rules the P08 rounds learned (restart the edge runtime after a `_shared` edit; `docker start` when the functions answer 503; Mailpit's port after a Docker restart; reset with both imports before an acceptance battery when test rows pile up; free memory before e2e; restore `next-env.d.ts` and remove `.next/e2e` after an e2e run), and how to run the P08 tests (unit, `vitest --mode db`, the e2e specs and which need the emulator).

No code changes. Run `pnpm check:copy` (it reads docs too if configured; if not, it is still run) and check every relative link you add resolves.
checks: a link check: a throwaway node command (not committed) that lists every relative markdown link in the four files and confirms each target exists; report what it printed
auditFocus: Truth against the code: every function, job, schedule, limit, code, column, environment name and Arabic button text named in the four documents exists exactly as named (spot-check at least thirty against the migrations and the functions). Nothing described that is not built; nothing built and owner-facing left out (each admin screen, each alert, each job). The 'When the Moyasar keys arrive' list complete against contract section 2's open items, and no claim that E02 or E03 is closed. The privacy map complete for every buyer table P08 created, with the true retention clocks. No secret value, no real address or name, no invented price or policy.
